content.title: About
content.content: Beef taco filling is a ready‑to‑heat mixture of ground beef, cheese, tomato and a specially seasoned taco sauce. It is designed for quick preparation of Mexican dishes such as tacos, burritos and fajitas.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Mexican taco filling is cooked on a skillet with chili, cumin and paprika spices.
The cheese blend often combines cheddar and mozzarella for optimal meltability.
Tomatoes give the filling a fresh, slightly tangy flavor and a vibrant color.
Taco sauce typically contains vinegar, sugar and aromatic spices, creating a sweet‑spicy balance.
The beef is usually browned until a golden crust forms, locking in juiciness.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Beef supplies easily absorbable heme iron, supporting healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both beef and cheese are good sources of B12, B6 and niacin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene from tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Beef and cheese can be high in saturated fats; people with elevated cholesterol should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Salt in the sauce
items.content: Taco sauce often contains a notable amount of sodium, so choose a reduced‑salt version if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper storage of the ready‑made filling can lead to bacterial growth; keep it refrigerated and observe use‑by dates.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the filling in a skillet or microwave, then spoon it into soft or crunchy taco shells. Top with fresh vegetables, guacamole, sour cream or salsa as desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3–5 days. For longer keeping, freeze in an airtight container for up to 2 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
